text: Four lessons, four pieces. This one puts them together into a single build, start to finish.

Answer the audience questions first. Keep only metrics that would actually change a decision, each with a real target. Sketch placement by reading order before building anything. Choose every visual against the distortion checklist, consistent scale and color throughout. Fit it to one screen, no scrollbars.

Here's that whole process, already finished. One card for the headline number. Charts that answer compared to what and broken down how. Nothing more detailed than an executive actually needs at a glance — and nothing left to a Power BI default.
Before calling it done, run the checklist one more time: does every tile trace back to a real need, does every KPI have a target, is the most important number the very first thing the eye lands on.
A well-designed dashboard still has to reach its audience — published, shared, kept current. That's exactly where Chapter Nine picks up: Power BI Service and Fabric.
